chunks: And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said: 'Has God sent a man as a messenger?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers reject the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) based on his humanity?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the principle of 'Bashariyyat' (humanity) of the Prophet, affirming that divine messengers are chosen from among humans to serve as relatable models for guidance. It addresses the Quraysh's objection that God would not send a mere mortal, highlighting the theological significance of the Prophet's dual nature as both divine representative and human exemplar. This reinforces the Shia belief in the infallibility and unique status of the Prophet while maintaining his essential humanity.
